Hi Anita — thanks for the clear note and the usage snapshot, that helps a lot.  I reviewed the export and sketched three pragmatic options below.  They’re designed to cover the common patterns we see (spikey tuning vs steady inference):

Option A — 21-day timebox extension (flat)
- One-off extension for +21 days, single flat price: $6,000 (list price $7,500; 20% pilot discount).
- No rollover (timebox ends on the new date).
- Includes 4 hours of priority onboarding/ops support.

Option B — Graded credit bucket (convertible)
- Three bands: Small (2k credits) = $2,200; Medium (6k credits) = $5,700; Large (15k credits) = $13,000.
- Unused credits can be rolled forward once (to a single 30‑day grace window) if you decide to convert to a paid plan within 60 days; otherwise unused credits expire.
- Credits non-refundable unless we mutually agree on exceptional circumstances (procurement typically accepts this for pilots).
- Includes 8 hours of engineering support for the first week if you select Medium or Large.

Option C — Short top-up (ad-hoc burst)
- One-off top-up at usage rates with a 10% volume discount for orders > $3k.
- No included support hours.

Notes / constraints:
- If you expect consistent high concurrency (sustained heavy load), we recommend evaluating Dedicated capacity — it requires a short provisioning window and separate quote.
- For bucket pricing we can offer a one-time concession of 15% on the Medium band (i.e., $4,845) for this pilot to help you finish tuning — subject to internal approval.

Next steps: tell me which option maps to your expected pattern (spike vs steady) and whether procurement needs a PO line or SOW. If helpful I can attach a short SOW and an itemized quote.

Best,
